sources.entry: tensorflow - An end-to-end machine learning platform from Google.

summary.one_liner: TensorFlow is Google's open source end-to-end platform for building and deploying machine learning models, with stable Python and C++ APIs.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes TensorFlow as an open source platform for machine learning with a broad ecosystem of tools, libraries, and community resources. It states that the framework was originally developed by Google Brain researchers and engineers and is general enough for use in other areas. It provides stable Python and C++ APIs and a non-guaranteed backward compatible API for other languages. The README covers pip installation of the main package (with CUDA GPU support on Ubuntu and Windows), a CPU-only package, and nightly builds. It also points to other device support through Device Plugins (DirectX and macOS Metal), a patching guide for release branches, and official build artifacts for Linux, macOS, Windows, Android (LiteRT), and Raspberry Pi.
use_cases: training neural networks and deep learning models
building ML models on Android via LiteRT
learning machine learning with tutorials and courses
notable: Stable Python and C++ APIs, with a non-guaranteed compatible API for other languages
Originally developed by Google Brain's Machine Intelligence team
GPU support for CUDA on Ubuntu and Windows, plus Device Plugins for DirectX and macOS Metal
Official builds for Linux, macOS, Windows, Android (LiteRT), and Raspberry Pi
Guidance for patching released versions by cherry-picking onto release branches
caveats: Non-Python/C++ language APIs are not backward compatible guaranteed
Some devices such as DirectX and macOS Metal require separate Device Plugins
Some official build artifacts are listed as TBA (Linux XLA)
